title: First visit to symnav — an outsider's system map

headings.text:
First, know
the place.
One terminal visit. A longer-lived workshop.

The workshop existed.
The ownership lines move.

Before
main

After
tip of #149
Production imports have a direction
Carry these six facts into every detail.
Retain preparation; renew meaning.
The host knows the product.
One owner for each rule.
Finishing bytes is different from doing work.
Accepted work has a continuing identity.
Preservation has a cost.

Know the choices
before the machinery.
State: which preparation survives another command?
Share the source-text cache without requiring TypeScript
Publish each prepared-file index only after preparation succeeds
Publish file-to-project membership as one graph
Let six query caches share a lifetime, not their contents
Give a workspace session to core
Host: who knows what a symnav command means?
Resolve the shared state directory at the CLI boundary
Load a host executor instead of importing the CLI from daemon code
Move start/status/stop formatting to renderer
Put the mechanism package behind DaemonClient
Switch the active CLI and enforce physical ownership
Policy and identity: who gets to decide?
Introduce the daemon package and one complete policy snapshot
Make every mechanism consume its policy section
Carry the command name; do not guess it from arguments
Separate worker failure from accepted-request failure
Make the first failed admission guard authoritative
Transport: who owns each part of the conversation?
Separate byte framing from protocol meaning
Retain receipt state across a resumed result fetch
Give raw outbound sockets one owner
Share the bounded, one-response exchange machinery
Give inbound connections their own server
Recover accepted execution in one client state machine
Make the remaining transport façade only compose and delegate
Daemon life: who keeps accepted work coherent?
Project status from explicit state snapshots
Give each worker lifetime an explicit generation
Coordinate delivery without taking ownership of ledger or spool data
Coordinate one FIFO turn per accepted identity
Tests, deferred behavior, and adjacent edits
The actual policy choices
Intentional absences

Follow one command
through the map.
Classify the question

A saved file is not
a saved answer.
Full refresh supplies a.ts and b.ts
The publication boundary is smaller than “the workspace”

Bring the answer back.
Keep the work's identity.
Same receiver. New socket.
Daemon process
Caller process
Six jobs the old transport façade held together
The worker can change while the daemon stays

Follow a claim
to the actual delta.
Explain where a second command's speed comes from, and why a broken socket doesn't mean “run it again.”
